title: Implementation Roadmap for Full Open Electricity Market for all Households
what_it_is: Implementation Roadmap for Full Open Electricity Market for all Households

sections.label: Open Electricity Market soft launch
sections.summary: Consumers may keep buying from SP Group at the regulated tariff, and the soft launch lets EMA, SP Group and retailers gather feedback before the market extends in the second half of 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Those who prefer to continue buying electricity from the SP Group at the regulated tariff can also continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This soft launch will allow the Energy Market Authority (EMA), the SP Group and electricity retailers to gather feedback and fine-tune their processes and backend systems before the Open Electricity Market is extended to the rest of Singapore in the second half of 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first is we do understand that the pilot is in Jurong and the areas demarcated by postal districts are, I understand, for the postal codes starting from 60 to 64.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask for the rest of the island, whether the plan is to also have staggered commencement based on postal districts or is everybody going to go live at the same time for the rest of the people outside Jurong?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: EMA had previously said that not all the retailers may be involved in the soft launch.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether there is any clarity now on whether certain specific retailers will be involved and whether this was their own choice or some vetting process by the EMA.

sections.label: Ofgem accreditation of information
sections.summary: The passage asks whether EMA is considering an accreditation role like Ofgem's so consumers have accurate information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An example is, I think, in the United Kingdom, where the Office of Gas and Electricity Markets (Ofgem) does this sort of accreditation of information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether the EMA, for example, is considering such an accreditation role, so that the consumers will have accurate information.

sections.label: Jurong pilot for electricity market
sections.summary: The exercise involves over a million accounts island-wide, so it focuses on one district like Jurong, reflecting household and business diversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the best of efforts and planning ahead, this is a massive exercise because it would involve over a million accounts, island-wide eventually, and that is why the idea of focusing it on one district or one area like Jurong, which in a way reflects the diversity or our household and business types.

sections.label: Pilot purpose and timeline
sections.summary: The pilot is held to see if anything unanticipated arises, and if it goes well the timeline towards complete implementation in the second half should hold.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is exactly why we are having the pilot to see if there is something unanticipated or something that is coming in from a different angle that we had not foreseen, and that is the purpose behind it.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, the answer is, if the pilot goes well, then I think we should be able to stick to the timeline and move towards the second half for complete implementation.

sections.label: Moving from businesses to households
sections.summary: Retailers currently deal with about 90,000 contestable market business accounts, and the move is now towards households.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The reason is because unlike the current situation where the retailers are essentially dealing with businesses who are in the contestable market – I understand it is about 90,000 accounts – we are now moving towards households.

sections.label: Online portal for price comparisons
sections.summary: The intent is to give consumers as much information as possible, including an online portal comparing different types of plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: On price comparisons or accreditation, the intent is to provide as much information as possible to consumers so that they can make informed decisions, and one part of that, apart from the general communications and media plan, is to have an online portal that will provide comparisons across different types of plans so that customers can then access this and then make the decisions based on their needs and they are informed by what these different plans offer.
